Consider the array-based implementation of Circular Queue.

int data[N];
int size =  front = rear = 0;

Here,

  • size is current size (number of elements) of queue.
  • $\textsf{N}$ is maximum size of queue.
  • front is an index to Front of queue and
  • rear is an index to rear of queue.

Let $\textsf{insert()}$ and $\textsf{remove()}$ are functions to insert and remove data items to or from the queue.

Which of the following is/are correct implementation of $\textsf{insert()}$ and $\textsf{remove()}?$

  1.   
    void insert(int item) {
    if ( (size == N )
        return;
    data[rear] = item;
    rear = (rear + 1) % N;
    size++;
}
  2.   
    void insert(int item) {
    if ( (size == N-1 )
        return;
    data[rear+1] = item;
    rear = (rear + 1) % N;
    size++;
}
  3.   
    int remove( ){
    int item = data[front];
    front = (front + 1) % N;
    size--;
    return item;
}
  4.   
    int remove( ){
    int item = data[front-1];
    front = (front + 1) % N;
    size--;
    return item;
}
